source: Confluence parent 562364446 (Bens Calls folder), 15 most recent Aircall transcripts pulled 2026-05-12 via Atlassian MCP
context: Ben Payne (HubSpot owner 76812243) is AgriProve's primary sales rep. This distillation runs parallel to Hobbs's call distillation to compare phone discipline (rapport vs pitch), cold-open style, value-prop deployment, and what each rep is setting up. Schema: pass0-farm-visit-distillation.md, but adapted for shorter call shapes.
lens: Ben vs Hobbs — does Ben pitch on the phone (compressed sales motion) or does he hold for visit (rapport infrastructure)?

topic_distillates.topic_label: Cold-open — first-name + 'Ben from AgriProof' on warm contact
topic_distillates.customer_position: Long-standing contact, in late-stage carbon project workflow.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Opens 'Hi, Alec. It's Ben from AgriProof. How are you?' — names AgriProve (mispronounced as AgriProof) in the second sentence. Apologises for time between conversations. No persona, no permission ask.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: It's Ben from AgriProof. How are you? // Sorry, it's been a little bit of time between conversations.

topic_distillates.customer_position: Customer mentions playing golf on Central Coast (where Ben lives); had been away playing golf.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Sustains 2+ minutes of golf-course chat: knows the local courses (Magenta, Chili Beats, Noraville), tells customer 'I'm just around the corner from there. I'm in Wombro,' offers next visit hospitality ('next time you're in the Central Coast, just give me a bell'). Personal-geography rapport is Ben's signature.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: Every time I talk to you, you're playing golf at the golf club. // Next time you're in the Central Coast, just give me a bell.

topic_distillates.topic_label: What Ben sets up — sequenced post-KCT close
topic_distillates.customer_position: Waiting for project documents; mentioned AgriWeb membership for records.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Sequences the next steps cleanly: 'We'll have everything to you by the end of the week as far as your carbon project plan and your key commercial terms... once we send that across for your review, then you take it down the avenues that you need to get checked off on... Will and I always like to do a post-KCT or key commercial terms catch up.' Names Will (Head of Ops) as the next touchpoint.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: We always like to do a post-KCT or key commercial terms catch up. // We've got all intentions to register the project, but we're a few steps away from that just yet.

visit_summary.one_line_summary: Maintained warmth in late-stage KCT shepherding via Central-Coast/golf rapport; cleanly sequenced post-KCT review with Head of Ops as next step.

topic_distillates.topic_label: Cold-open — names AgriProve + Albury geography immediately
topic_distillates.customer_position: Stud-operator answering with company name; no prior contact with AgriProve.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Opens with 'Ben calling here from AgriProve in Albury. How's things?' AgriProve named in sentence one. Frames the call as a 'regional outreach program based out of Aubrey... looking at what's working across the Riverina as far as grazing operations.'
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: It's Ben calling here from AgriProve in Albury. // Your property has actually come up as one of those identified.

topic_distillates.topic_label: The Hobbs intro — 'gentleman from The US, paddock conversation'
topic_distillates.customer_position: Asks what Hobbs would like to discuss / what the objective is.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Frames Hobbs as 'a gentleman out here from The US who's a guy by the name of Hobbs Magaret, who's just looking to have a bit of a paddock conversation on practical grazing methods.' Soft, low-commitment framing — 'paddock conversation' not 'sales meeting.' Mentions soil health and grazing management 'go hand in hand.'
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: A gentleman out here from The US... just looking to have a bit of a paddock conversation on practical grazing methods.

topic_distillates.topic_label: Visit booked — same call, specific slot
topic_distillates.customer_position: Open to Friday next week; checks distance from Albury.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Books 11am Friday 15th in-call. No carbon pitch, no ACCU mention, no methodology, no revenue split. Pure visit-booking. Will email meeting request + Hobbs's phone number.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: I'll send through his phone number as well too and just a meeting request for 11:00 on the fifteenth.

visit_summary.one_line_summary: Cold outreach to Riverina stud-operator booked Hobbs farm visit in 3 minutes; zero value-prop deployment — pure visit-booking discipline.

topic_distillates.customer_position: Operator gently probes 'when you say Riverina, where do you think I am? Have you got the right person?'
topic_distillates.ben_response: Owns the awkwardness without polish: 'that's also the ultimate question here. So I don't have... I've got you in Vic, but I'm not too sure where.' Doesn't try to bluff. Asks about size.

visit_summary.one_line_summary: Soft-curious operator handled with information-share + Google-Hobbs validation path; visit not yet booked but warmly progressing.

topic_distillates.customer_position: Late-stage skeptical operator who just received KCT/responses document.
topic_distillates.ben_response: 'Hi, Brian. It's Ben calling here from AgriProof. How are you going?' Brief small-talk. Quickly pivots to 'I just shot you a text this morning. We've sent across all the responses... make sure they landed with you okay.'
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: I just shot you a text this morning. We've sent across all the responses to both Kevin and you.

topic_distillates.customer_position: 'I'm not instilled with confidence in it... when the word may is used, may doesn't stand any shit at all... I don't wanna lock anything up for twenty five years because you can't tell me what's gonna happen in the future. You can't tell me what the government is gonna do.'
topic_distillates.ben_response: Tries to defuse 'lock up' framing — 'We're not locking up land. We're not in the business of locking up land. I know that word gets bandied around a little bit, but there's no locking up a land.' But doesn't deploy Hobbs's clean Tier-1 framings (e.g., 'two clauses' or 'we don't do trees'). Defaults to procedural reassurance ('there are caveats in there', 'we can review this after a five year period').
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: We're not locking up land. We're not in the business of locking up land. // There are caveats in there a 100%. We can review this after a five year period.

topic_distillates.customer_position: 'If the government changes hands tomorrow, there's no nothing written in cement here that I'm gonna get paid in it... $37. That can drop, and that can up and down.'
topic_distillates.ben_response: Cites Abbott's failed abolition attempt: 'I think Abbott tried to abolish it as well too, and that didn't fly... there's been too many attempts at it, and the market's too big to warrant any any change there.' This is a Ben-specific historical/political defence — Hobbs uses 'carbon tax alternative' (#7) instead.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: I think Abbott tried to abolish it as well too, and that didn't fly. The market's too big to warrant any change there.

topic_distillates.customer_position: 'You take 25% of that every year. Am I right or wrong?'
topic_distillates.ben_response: Doesn't use Hobbs's killer reframe ('25% of what you weren't going to get anything from before'). Instead defaults to cost-justification: 'It's 25% of the ACCUs, which covers all of our costs for the entirety of the lifespan of the project... those audits cost us $30 alone... there's so much compliancy admin, there's so much cost involved for us to set this up.' Cost-defence rather than re-frame.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: 25% of the ACCUs covers all of our costs for the entirety of the lifespan of the project. Those audits cost us $30 alone.

topic_distillates.customer_position: Concerned about going backwards in carbon stocks.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Explains the ratchet correctly: 'When we do the baseline... once the project starts to take over, year one, once you see an increase above the baseline... If that dips in year two, if you go backwards — and this is one of the biggest misconceptions of soil carbon projects — the minute you go backwards, there's no penalty. There's no paying back of credits.' Hobbs-aligned framing, just less crisp than 'It works on a ratchet... boom, you get credited.'
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: The minute you go backwards, there's no penalty. There's no paying back of credits. It's one of the biggest misinformation pieces.

topic_distillates.topic_label: Close — defer to think, no push

topic_distillates.ben_response: 'No, I understand that. Totally understand that. No problem at all. I'll leave that with you, and I'll come back to you with any kind of concerns I can quash.' No forcing. But no clean concrete next step either.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: I'll leave that with you, and I'll come back to you with any kind of concerns I can quash, I'll come back with you on it.

visit_summary.one_line_summary: Late-stage QLD skeptic re-surfaced 25%/25-year/government-risk objections after KCT review; Ben handled defensively without Hobbs's Tier-1 reframes — call ended ambiguously, customer needs time.

topic_distillates.customer_position: Long-paused prospect with prior contract-flexibility concerns.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Opens 'Just sort of touch base with you and just, obviously, things have changed a lot now... wanted to sort of touch base.' Then frames the change: 'I guess probably the major change is around sort of flexibility. I know there were sort of a couple of sort of concerns at your end, but we have made some significant strides... in the flexibility of our contracts and the way we sort of review things after a five year period. It's an annualized review.'
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: Things have changed a lot now. // The major change is around sort of flexibility. We've made some significant strides in the flexibility of our contracts and an annualized review.

topic_distillates.customer_position: Listens, asking cost questions.
topic_distillates.ben_response: Deploys full Horizon backstory on phone: '$12,000,000 investment that has been injected back into the business... using sophisticated satellite technology, which is a massive upgrade from the NDRE technology... 20 to 30,000 soil sets from live projects... washing it against topography and other scientific layers... understand your carbon stocks on a monthly basis... annual crediting system.' This is the heaviest value-prop deployment in the whole 15-call set.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: Roughly $12,000,000 investment injected back into the business. // 20 to 30,000 soil sets from live projects. Understand your carbon stocks on a monthly basis.

topic_distillates.customer_position: 'What's your sort of data... do you guys go to set percentage for The UK?'
topic_distillates.ben_response: Clean answer: 'You keep 75% of the credits. The 25% for us covers every single cost for the life of the project. So the only cost to you is the baselining.' This is Ben's standard split framing — closer to Hobbs's Tier-1 #1 in clarity but without the 'taking 25% of what you weren't going to get anything from before' reframe punch.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: You keep 75% of the credits. The 25% for us covers every single cost for the life of the project.

topic_distillates.customer_position: Concerned about 'how restricted they'll be on management... I don't wanna get five or ten years down the road and be like, this really needs to happen, but I'm restricted.'
topic_distillates.ben_response: Reassures via process: 'We do cover all that in what we call a land management strategy call... 12 different practices, you only have to choose a maximum of two... we're not here to tell you how to do your practices. It's very much led by you, entire journey.' Hobbs's 'we let you guys farm the way you think you should farm' lite — Ben uses 'led by you' instead.
topic_distillates.quotable_phrasing: We're not here to tell you how to do your practices. It's very much led by you, entire journey. // We're here to run the race with you, besides you.
